questions.stem: Tessellate's RIQ API has an availability SLO of 99.9% over 28 days. Halfway through the window, 80% of the error budget is spent. What does an SRE error budget policy typically prescribe?
options: Ignore it until the window ends
Slow or freeze risky feature releases and prioritize reliability work until the budget recovers
questions.explanation: The budget balances velocity and reliability; when it is nearly gone, releases slow down and reliability work takes priority.

questions.stem: Which SLI best reflects user experience for the RIQ query API?
options: Proportion of valid requests served successfully under the latency threshold, measured at the load balancer or service
questions.explanation: SLIs measure what users feel: availability and latency of good requests, as close to the user as practical.

questions.stem: You want a metric of how often MDM logs `ERROR import failed` and to alert on it. What is the native approach?
options: Create a log-based counter metric with a filter on that entry and an alerting policy on the metric
Add a Prometheus exporter that reads Cloud Logging
Export logs to a VM and grep
questions.explanation: Log-based metrics turn matching log entries into time series you can alert on.

questions.stem: Security wants every project's audit logs retained centrally for a year, including new projects. Choose two.
options: Set the destination bucket's retention to the required period and restrict access to it
Create a sink in each project by hand
Create an aggregated sink at the organization (or folder) with child resources included, routing to a central log bucket or storage
Rely on the default project retention
Export logs from the console monthly
questions.explanation: Aggregated sinks cover existing and future projects; retention and access control live at the destination.

questions.stem: You need managed promotion of a release from stg-1 to prod-blue with a manual approval and rollback. Which GCP service fits best?
options: Cloud Deploy, with a delivery pipeline whose prod target requires approval
questions.explanation: Cloud Deploy models delivery pipelines and targets, promotions, approvals and rollbacks for GKE and Cloud Run.

questions.stem: Cloud Build must reach a private GKE control plane and an internal artifact mirror. What do you use?
options: Default Cloud Build workers with public IPs
Cloud Build private pools peered to your VPC
Cloud NAT on the default pool
questions.explanation: Private pools run in a Google-managed network peered to yours, giving builds private connectivity.

questions.stem: Which is the least-privilege way for Cloud Build to deploy to tsl-riq-prod?
options: Run the trigger as a user-specified service account that holds only the deploy roles it needs in the target project
Store a key in the repo
Give the default Cloud Build service account project owner
questions.explanation: Per-pipeline service accounts with narrow roles are the recommended model.

learn.label: Best practices for using service accounts

questions.stem: A canary of riq-api v2 receives 10% of traffic. Error rate on the canary is 3x the baseline. What should the process do?
options: Stop and roll back the canary automatically based on the comparison with the baseline
questions.explanation: Canary analysis compares canary and baseline; a regression aborts the rollout.

questions.stem: A Deployment's pods are killed during node upgrades mid-request. Which change helps most?
options: Handle SIGTERM: fail readiness, drain in-flight requests within terminationGracePeriodSeconds (a preStop hook if needed), plus a PDB
questions.explanation: Graceful termination and a PDB make node maintenance invisible to users.

questions.stem: prod-green must not receive minor upgrades during a two-week launch, but should still get security patches. What do you configure?
options: A no-minor-upgrades maintenance exclusion covering the launch
questions.explanation: No-minor-upgrades keeps patches flowing.

questions.stem: During a major incident, which two roles from Google's incident management practice should be explicit? Choose two.
options: Communications lead who keeps stakeholders updated
Incident commander who coordinates and delegates
questions.explanation: Clear roles (IC, ops, comms) prevent freelancing and keep stakeholders informed.

questions.stem: Your on-call team spends 60% of its time on manual certificate renewals and import requests. What does SRE guidance say?
options: Toil should be capped (Google targets under 50% of SRE time); automate the repetitive work and measure the hours saved
questions.explanation: Google SRE aims to keep toil below half of an engineer's time and invest the rest in engineering that removes it.

questions.stem: You need to know if the public RIQ endpoint is reachable from several regions. What do you set up?
options: Uptime check against the endpoint with an alerting policy
questions.explanation: Uptime checks probe from multiple locations and alert on failures.

questions.stem: Developers want to see where latency is spent across MDM microservices. What do you recommend?
options: Distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry instrumentation exported to Cloud Trace (through a Collector)
questions.explanation: Traces show per-hop latency; OTel keeps instrumentation vendor-neutral.

questions.stem: A team on GKE wants Prometheus metrics without running Prometheus servers. What do you offer?
options: Managed Service for Prometheus with managed collection (PodMonitoring), queried with PromQL in Cloud Monitoring or Grafana
questions.explanation: GMP keeps PromQL and the Prometheus model while Google runs the storage and collectors.

learn.label: Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus

questions.stem: An image with a critical CVE is running in prod. Where do you look to find which images and digests are affected across projects?
options: Artifact Analysis vulnerability occurrences for Artifact Registry images (and Security Command Center findings at org level)
questions.explanation: Artifact Analysis records vulnerabilities per digest; SCC aggregates findings.

questions.stem: A Compute Engine VM in tsl-rdm-prod needs to read a bucket. How should it authenticate?
options: An attached user-managed service account with only the needed role; the metadata server provides short-lived tokens
The default compute service account with editor
questions.explanation: Attached service accounts with least privilege avoid keys; the default compute SA historically had broad roles.

learn.label: Best practices for using service accounts

questions.stem: Which statement about IAM role types is correct?
options: Predefined roles are curated per service; custom roles fit when no predefined role is narrow enough; basic roles are too broad for production
Predefined roles cannot be bound at folder level
Basic roles (owner, editor, viewer) are recommended for production
Custom roles can be created only at project level
questions.explanation: Prefer predefined, then custom; avoid basic roles.

questions.stem: Your CI applies Terraform. How do you prevent two pipelines from corrupting the state of the network stack?
options: Ask people not to run at the same time
Use a remote backend with locking (GCS) and run applies only from the pipeline
questions.explanation: Remote state with locking and a single apply path.

questions.stem: After an incident, leadership asks for a blameless postmortem. What does blameless mean in practice?
options: Focus on how the system and process allowed the failure and fix those, assuming people acted reasonably with the information they had
questions.explanation: Blameless postmortems surface the real contributing causes.

questions.stem: Cluster autoscaler scales riq-api nodes slowly at 08:00 every weekday. What is a cost-aware fix?
options: Scheduled scaling of replicas before the known peak, or keep modest headroom; right-size requests so scaling decisions are accurate
questions.explanation: Predictable peaks favor scheduled scaling; accurate requests drive both cost and scheduling.

questions.stem: Which two belong in a good alerting policy for a paging alert? Choose two.
options: It links to a runbook and is routed to the on-call rotation
It is tied to user-facing symptoms or SLO burn, not every cause metric
It fires on any single error
questions.explanation: Page on symptoms with runbooks; send causes and warnings to tickets or dashboards.

questions.stem: Prod should reject images not attested by the CI attestor, but a vendor DaemonSet image cannot be attested. What do you configure?
options: An allowlist (exempt image pattern) for that specific vendor image path in the policy, reviewed and documented
questions.explanation: Binary Authorization policies support exempt image patterns for images you cannot attest; keep them narrow.

questions.stem: Billing for tsl-sandbox-legacy spiked. Where do you start?
options: Billing reports and cost breakdown by service and SKU, then labels or GKE cost allocation to attribute it, and budgets with alerts to catch it next time
questions.explanation: Attribute, then prevent with budgets and alerts.

questions.stem: Which practice best reduces the risk of a change causing an outage on the platform?
options: Progressive rollouts with automated health checks and quick rollback, plus change records tied to deploys
questions.explanation: Most outages follow changes; progressive delivery limits blast radius.
